title: Short-exact devissage for the eight assertions
statement:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-algebraic-closure], let $C$ be a separated scheme of finite type over $k$ with $\dim C\le1$, and let

$$
 0\longrightarrow F_1\xrightarrow{\ \alpha\ }F\xrightarrow{\ \beta\ }F_2\longrightarrow0
$$

be a short exact sequence in the abelian category $\Ab(C_{\Et})$ of abelian sheaves on the small etale site [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves] in which $F_1$ and $F_2$ are torsion [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves], so that $(C,F_1)$ and $(C,F_2)$ are curve coefficient pairs [def-weil-pbc-curve-setting]. Then $F$ is torsion, so $(C,F)$ is a curve coefficient pair. For a curve coefficient pair $(C,G)$ read each of the eight assertions $\mathcal C_j(C,G)$ of [def-weil-pbc-eight-curve-assertions] as an implication about this pair: its conclusion is asserted whenever its hypotheses (on $C$, on $\operatorname{char}k$, on $G$, and for every algebraically closed extension $k'/k$, every open immersion $a:U\hookrightarrow C$ and every degree $q$ in its range) are met, and it holds when they fail (Stacks, Situation 0A52). If $\mathcal C(C,F_1)$ and $\mathcal C(C,F_2)$ hold, then $\mathcal C(C,F)$ holds. In particular the class of torsion abelian sheaves $G$ on $C_{\Et}$ with $\mathcal C(C,G)$ is closed under extensions.

proof.text: *$F$ is torsion.* Torsion means [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves]: every local section is locally killed by a positive integer. Since the sequence is exact, $\alpha$ is a kernel of $\beta$, and kernels in $\Ab(C_{\Et})$ are computed sectionwise [def-pur-abelian-sheaf-kernel]: for every etale $V\to C$, $0\to F_1(V)\xrightarrow{\alpha_V}F(V)\xrightarrow{\beta_V}F_2(V)$ is exact. Let $s\in F(V)$. As $F_2$ is torsion, there are an etale covering $\{V_i\to V\}$ and integers $n_i\ge1$ with $n_i\beta(s)|_{V_i}=0$, i.e. $\beta_{V_i}(n_is|_{V_i})=0$; so $n_is|_{V_i}=\alpha_{V_i}(t_i)$ for a unique $t_i\in F_1(V_i)$. As $F_1$ is torsion, there are coverings $\{V_{ij}\to V_i\}$ and integers $m_{ij}\ge1$ with $m_{ij}t_i|_{V_{ij}}=0$, hence $m_{ij}n_is|_{V_{ij}}=\alpha(m_{ij}t_i|_{V_{ij}})=0$. The composite family $\{V_{ij}\to V\}$ is an etale covering (coverings of the site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site] are stable under composition), so $s$ is locally killed by the positive integers $m_{ij}n_i$. Hence $F$ is torsion and $(C,F)$ is a curve coefficient pair [def-weil-pbc-curve-setting].

source.place: Etale Cohomology, proof of Lemma 0A5C (lemma-ses-statements); the hypothesis 'short exact sequence of torsion abelian sheaves', where Stacks assumes all three terms torsion; that the middle term is torsion when the outer ones are is written out here

proof.text: *The hypotheses on the sheaf pass from $F$ to $F_1$ and $F_2$* (the point Stacks settles by Proposition 09BH). (a) *Torsion conditions.* Let $\bar c$ be a geometric point of $C$. The stalk functor at $\bar c$ [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks] is exact [prop-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks-exact], so $0\to(F_1)_{\bar c}\to F_{\bar c}\to(F_2)_{\bar c}\to0$ is an exact sequence of abelian groups: $(F_1)_{\bar c}$ is isomorphic to a subgroup of $F_{\bar c}$ and $(F_2)_{\bar c}$ to a quotient of it. If every element of $F_{\bar c}$ is killed by a power of $p$ (resp. has finite order prime to $p$), the same holds for every element of a subgroup and of a quotient (the order of the image of $x$ divides the order of $x$). Since being $p$-primary or prime to $p$ is defined stalkwise [def-weil-pbc-primary-torsion], $F$ $p$-primary implies $F_1,F_2$ $p$-primary, and $F$ prime to $\operatorname{char}k$ implies $F_1,F_2$ prime to $\operatorname{char}k$ (in characteristic $0$ the latter is no condition). (b) *Constructibility.* If $F$ is constructible [def-weil-pbc-constructible-torsion], then so are $F_1$ and $F_2$ by [lem-weil-pbc-curve-constructible-sub-quotient] (all three terms are torsion by the hypothesis and step 1). (c) The conditions on $C$ ($C$ affine, $C$ proper over $k$) and on $\operatorname{char}k$ are the same for $F$, $F_1$, $F_2$. Consequently: whenever the hypotheses of one of the assertions $\mathcal C_3,\mathcal C_4,\mathcal C_5,\mathcal C_6$ [def-weil-pbc-C3], [def-weil-pbc-C4], [def-weil-pbc-C5], [def-weil-pbc-C6] hold for $(C,F)$, the hypotheses of the same assertion hold for $(C,F_1)$ and $(C,F_2)$; the assertions $\mathcal C_1,\mathcal C_2,\mathcal C_7,\mathcal C_8$ have no hypothesis on the sheaf.

source.place: Etale Cohomology, proof of Lemma 0A5C (lemma-ses-statements); 'Also observe that F is constructible (resp. of torsion prime to the characteristic of k) if and only if both F_1 and F_2 are ... See Proposition 09BH (proposition-constructible-over-noetherian)'; only the direction from F to F_1, F_2 is used, and the p-primary case is added

proof.text:
*The long exact sequences and their naturality.* Apply [lem-weil-pbc-pullback-cohomology-long-exact-ladder] to the short exact sequence $0\to F_1\xrightarrow{\alpha}F\xrightarrow{\beta}F_2\to0$ on $C_{\Et}$ and a morphism of schemes $u:Y\to C$ (below $u=\mathrm{id}_C$, the projection $\pi:C_{k'}\to C$, or an open immersion $a:U\hookrightarrow C$). Clause 1: $0\to u^{-1}F_1\xrightarrow{u^{-1}\alpha}u^{-1}F\xrightarrow{u^{-1}\beta}u^{-1}F_2\to0$ is exact on $Y_{\Et}$. Clause 2: there are connecting maps $\delta^q_C$, $\delta^q_Y$ making
$$0\to H^0(C,F_1)\to\cdots\to H^q(C,F_1)\xrightarrow{H^q(\alpha)}H^q(C,F)\xrightarrow{H^q(\beta)}H^q(C,F_2)\xrightarrow{\delta^q_C}H^{q+1}(C,F_1)\to\cdots$$
exact, and likewise on $Y$ for $u^{-1}F_1,u^{-1}F,u^{-1}F_2$ (cohomology groups of [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology], $H^q(\varphi)$ the maps of [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback-functorial]). Clause 3: the pullback maps $u^*$ of [def-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback] satisfy $u^*H^q(\alpha)=H^q(u^{-1}\alpha)u^*$, $u^*H^q(\beta)=H^q(u^{-1}\beta)u^*$ and $u^*\delta^q_C=\delta^q_Yu^*$ for all $q\ge0$. For the vanishing and finiteness assertions only the sequence on $C$ is used (take $u=\mathrm{id}_C$, or simply the $C$-part of clause 2).

source.place: Etale Cohomology, proof of Lemma 0A5C (lemma-ses-statements); 'the long exact sequence of cohomology'

proof.text: *Vanishing: $\mathcal C_1,\mathcal C_2,\mathcal C_3$.* Let $q$ be in the range of one of these assertions for $(C,F)$: $q>2$ for [def-weil-pbc-C1]; $C$ affine and $q>1$ for [def-weil-pbc-C2]; $\operatorname{char}k=p>0$, $F$ $p$-primary and $q>1$ for [def-weil-pbc-C3]. By step 2 the hypotheses of the same assertion hold for $(C,F_1)$ and $(C,F_2)$, so $\mathcal C(C,F_1)$ and $\mathcal C(C,F_2)$ give $H^q(C,F_1)=0$ and $H^q(C,F_2)=0$. The segment $H^q(C,F_1)\xrightarrow{H^q(\alpha)}H^q(C,F)\xrightarrow{H^q(\beta)}H^q(C,F_2)$ of step 3 is exact at $H^q(C,F)$: for $x\in H^q(C,F)$, $H^q(\beta)(x)\in H^q(C,F_2)=0$, so $x\in\ker H^q(\beta)=\operatorname{im}H^q(\alpha)=0$. Hence $H^q(C_{\Et},F)=0$.

source.place: Etale Cohomology, proof of Lemma 0A5C (lemma-ses-statements); statements (1)-(3) of Situation 0A52 for the middle term

proof.text: *Finiteness: $\mathcal C_4,\mathcal C_5$.* Assume $F$ constructible and prime to $\operatorname{char}k$ (for [def-weil-pbc-C4]), resp. $C$ proper over $k$ and $F$ constructible (for [def-weil-pbc-C5]). By step 2, $F_1$ and $F_2$ satisfy the same hypotheses, so $\mathcal C(C,F_1)$, $\mathcal C(C,F_2)$ make $H^q(C,F_1)$ and $H^q(C,F_2)$ finite for every $q\ge0$. The sequence $H^q(C,F_1)\xrightarrow{H^q(\alpha)}H^q(C,F)\xrightarrow{H^q(\beta)}H^q(C,F_2)$ is exact at $H^q(C,F)$ for every $q\ge0$ (step 3), so $H^q(C,F)$ is finite by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-middle-of-exact] (it is an extension of the subgroup $\operatorname{im}H^q(\beta)$ of $H^q(C,F_2)$ by the quotient $\operatorname{im}H^q(\alpha)$ of $H^q(C,F_1)$), for every $q\ge0$.

source.place: Etale Cohomology, proof of Lemma 0A5C (lemma-ses-statements); statements (4), (5) of Situation 0A52 for the middle term

proof.text: *Invariance: $\mathcal C_6,\mathcal C_7$.* Assume $F$ prime to $\operatorname{char}k$ (for [def-weil-pbc-C6]) or $C$ proper over $k$ (for [def-weil-pbc-C7]); fix an algebraically closed extension $k'/k$ and let $\pi:C_{k'}=C\times_kk'\to C$ be the projection. The map $\rho^q_{k'/k}(C,G)$ of [def-weil-pbc-extension-pullback] is the pullback map $\pi^*:H^q(C_{\Et},G)\to H^q((C_{k'})_{\Et},\pi^{-1}G)$ of [def-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback] for $u=\pi$, with $G_{k'}=\pi^{-1}G$. By step 2 (resp. since $C$ is proper), the same assertion holds for $(C,F_1)$ and $(C,F_2)$: $\rho^q_{k'/k}(C,F_1)$ and $\rho^q_{k'/k}(C,F_2)$ are bijective for every $q\ge0$. Apply step 3 with $u=\pi$: $0\to\pi^{-1}F_1\to\pi^{-1}F\to\pi^{-1}F_2\to0$ is exact on $(C_{k'})_{\Et}$, both long sequences are exact, and the maps $\pi^*$ commute with $H^q(\alpha),H^q(\beta),\delta^q$ and their counterparts. Fix $q\ge0$ and consider the commutative diagram of abelian groups with top row $H^{q-1}(C,F_2)\xrightarrow{\delta^{q-1}_C}H^q(C,F_1)\xrightarrow{H^q(\alpha)}H^q(C,F)\xrightarrow{H^q(\beta)}H^q(C,F_2)\xrightarrow{\delta^q_C}H^{q+1}(C,F_1)$, bottom row the same on $C_{k'}$ for $\pi^{-1}F_1,\pi^{-1}F,\pi^{-1}F_2$, and the five vertical maps $\pi^*$; for $q=0$ the first entry of each row is replaced by $0$ (and the first vertical map by $0\to0$), which keeps the rows exact because the long exact sequences begin with $0\to H^0(-_1)$. The squares commute by clause 3 (the first trivially for $q=0$) and the rows are exact at the three middle places by clause 2. The four outer vertical maps are bijective: $\pi^*$ on $H^{q-1}(F_2)$ and $H^q(F_2)$ by the assertion for $F_2$, on $H^q(F_1)$ and $H^{q+1}(F_1)$ by the assertion for $F_1$ (this uses the assertions for $F_1,F_2$ in the degrees $q-1,q,q+1$, which is why they are asserted for every $q$). Bijective homomorphisms are the isomorphisms of $\Ab$, so the five lemma [lem-weil-pbc-five-lemma] makes $\rho^q_{k'/k}(C,F)=\pi^*$ bijective. As $k'$ and $q$ were arbitrary, $\mathcal C_6(C,F)$, resp. $\mathcal C_7(C,F)$, holds.

source.place: Etale Cohomology, proof of Lemma 0A5C (lemma-ses-statements); statements (6), (7) of Situation 0A52 for the middle term: the pullback to X_{k'} of the long exact sequence and the five lemma (pattern of the reviewed lem-weil-pbc-pullback-iso-prime-torsion-devissage, step 2)

proof.text: *Surjectivity: $\mathcal C_8$.* Let $a:U\hookrightarrow C$ be an open immersion. The restriction map $a^*:H^2(C_{\Et},G)\to H^2(U_{\Et},a^{-1}G)$ of [def-weil-pbc-C8] is the pullback map of [def-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback] for $u=a$ (clause 5 of [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback-functorial] identifies it with $\mathcal H^2$ of the restriction of an injective resolution); it is a homomorphism. Apply step 3 with $u=a$, writing $\alpha_U=a^{-1}\alpha$, $\beta_U=a^{-1}\beta$: the sequence $H^2(U,a^{-1}F_1)\xrightarrow{H^2(\alpha_U)}H^2(U,a^{-1}F)\xrightarrow{H^2(\beta_U)}H^2(U,a^{-1}F_2)$ is exact, $H^2(C,F)\xrightarrow{H^2(\beta)}H^2(C,F_2)\xrightarrow{\delta^2_C}H^3(C,F_1)$ is exact, and $a^*H^2(\alpha)=H^2(\alpha_U)a^*$, $a^*H^2(\beta)=H^2(\beta_U)a^*$. Let $y\in H^2(U_{\Et},a^{-1}F)$ and $y_2=H^2(\beta_U)(y)$. (i) By $\mathcal C_8(C,F_2)$ there is $x_2\in H^2(C,F_2)$ with $a^*x_2=y_2$. (ii) $\delta^2_C(x_2)\in H^3(C,F_1)$, which is $0$ by $\mathcal C_1(C,F_1)$ [def-weil-pbc-C1] ($3>2$); so $x_2\in\ker\delta^2_C=\operatorname{im}H^2(\beta)$: choose $x\in H^2(C,F)$ with $H^2(\beta)(x)=x_2$. (iii) $H^2(\beta_U)(y-a^*x)=y_2-a^*H^2(\beta)(x)=y_2-a^*x_2=0$, so by exactness there is $y_1\in H^2(U,a^{-1}F_1)$ with $H^2(\alpha_U)(y_1)=y-a^*x$. (iv) By $\mathcal C_8(C,F_1)$ there is $x_1\in H^2(C,F_1)$ with $a^*x_1=y_1$. (v) Then $a^*\bigl(x+H^2(\alpha)(x_1)\bigr)=a^*x+H^2(\alpha_U)(a^*x_1)=a^*x+(y-a^*x)=y$. So $a^*:H^2(C_{\Et},F)\to H^2(U_{\Et},a^{-1}F)$ is surjective; no condition on $U$ or on the sheaf is used. This is $\mathcal C_8(C,F)$.

proof.text: *Conclusion.* Steps 4 to 7 give each of the eight assertions for the curve coefficient pair $(C,F)$ (step 1) whenever its hypotheses are met, i.e. $\mathcal C(C,F)$ [def-weil-pbc-eight-curve-assertions]. The last sentence of the statement is a restatement: if $G_1,G_2$ are torsion with $\mathcal C(C,G_1)$, $\mathcal C(C,G_2)$ and $0\to G_1\to G\to G_2\to0$ is exact, then $G$ is torsion and $\mathcal C(C,G)$ holds.

blueprint_sketch.statement:
Let

$$
0\longrightarrow F_1\xrightarrow{a}F\xrightarrow{b}F_2\longrightarrow0
$$

be exact. If all applicable assertions $\mathcal C_r(X,F_i)$ hold for
$i=1,2$, then all applicable assertions hold for $F$.
blueprint_sketch.proof:
Pullback to an extension field is exact, so the displayed sequence and its
base change give natural long exact cohomology sequences.

For (1), (2), and (3), in every degree above the stated bound the exact
segment

$$
H^q(X,F_1)\xrightarrow{a_*}H^q(X,F)
\xrightarrow{b_*}H^q(X,F_2)
$$

has zero end terms. Hence its middle term is zero. The hypotheses on
affineness and characteristic are unchanged, and in (3) an extension of two
$p$-power torsion sheaves is again killed by a power of $p$.

For (4) and (5), constructible sheaves form a Serre subcategory: on a common
finite stratification the stalk sequence is an exact sequence of finite
groups. Prime-to-characteristic torsion is also preserved by extensions.
Exactness identifies $H^q(X,F)$ as an extension of
$\operatorname{im}a_*$ by $\operatorname{im}b_*$; these are respectively a
quotient of the finite group $H^q(X,F_1)$ and a subgroup of the finite group
$H^q(X,F_2)$. Thus $H^q(X,F)$ is finite.

For (6) and (7), write the long exact sequence for $F_1,F,F_2$ above its
base-changed sequence. Every square commutes because restriction commutes
with $a$, $b$, and the boundary map obtained from an injective resolution.
For fixed $q$, the four outer vertical arrows in the five-term portion

$$
H^{q-1}(F_2)\to H^q(F_1)\to H^q(F)\to H^q(F_2)\to H^{q+1}(F_1)
$$

are isomorphisms; the five lemma makes the middle arrow an isomorphism.

For (8), let $c\in H^2(W,F|_W)$ and put $c_2=b_*(c)$. Choose
$x_2\in H^2(X,F_2)$ restricting to $c_2$. Its boundary lies in
$H^3(X,F_1)=0$ by (1), so exactness gives
$x\in H^2(X,F)$ with $b_*(x)=x_2$. The difference
$c-x|_W$ maps to zero in $H^2(W,F_2|_W)$, hence equals $a_*(d_1)$ for some
$d_1\in H^2(W,F_1|_W)$. Choose $y_1\in H^2(X,F_1)$ restricting to $d_1$.
Then $x+a_*(y_1)$ restricts to $c$. This proves the eighth assertion and
completes all eight cases compressed in Tag `0A5C`.
